--absolute.help: Pad inputs to be at least N bytes in size.

--agent.help: Produce a unit overview for AI agents.

--all.help: Search full help output (not just unit descriptions).

--and.help: Require all keywords to match rather than any of them matching.

--ascii.help: Read the memory at the given offset as an ASCII string.

--blocksize.help: The size of each block in bytes, default is 1.

--brief.help: List units with a one-line description only.

--bytes.help: hide instruction bytes next to disassembly

--chunk-size.help: Optionally specify the chunk size for compression, default is 0x1000.

--conjunctive.help: All keywords must match rather than any of them.

--delta.help: Add a delta filter when compressing.

--dos.help: Use DOS time parser instead of Unix time stamp parser.

--end.help: Read bytes until this offset, which has to be located after the starting offset.

--epilogue.help: Optional expression with which the state variable S is updated after a block was operated on.

--esc.help: Always peek data as string, escape characters if necessary.

--expand.help: Do not compress sequences of identical lines in hexdump

--force.help: decompress even if all known methods fail

--format.help: Provide format strings instead of a list of filenames. The format strings will be used cyclically to generate a file name for each input to be dumped.

--help.help: Show this help message and exit.

--hex.help: Hex encode everything, do not use C escape sequences.

--hexdump.help: Only look for exactly two digit hexadecimal numbers surrounded by whitespace.

--iff.help: Only apply unit if it can handle the input format. Specify twice to drop all other chunks.

--ignore-unknown.help: Unless this option is set, the key stream will be iterated even for letters that are not contained in the alphabet.

--indent.help: Controls the amount of space characters used for indentation in the output. Default is 4.

--iv.help: Specifies the initialization vector. If none is specified, then a block of zero bytes is used.

--keep-references.help: Do not resolve Object references in serialized data.

--left.help: Pad on the left instead of the right.

--len.help: If this flag is specified, the size parameter determines the number of blocks to be produced rather than the size of each block.

--lenient.help: Increase the leniency, allowing partial results and ignoring more errors.

--lines.help: Specify number N of lines in the preview, default is 10.

--lines-all.help: Output all possible preview lines without restriction

--little-endian.help: use little endian instead of the default big endian byte order.

--longest.help: Sort results by length before picking.

--max.help: Matches must have length at most N.

--min.help: Matches must have length at least N.

--nbo.help: Read chunks in network byte order (big endian).

--no-addr.help: Do not show byte offsets in hexdump.

--no-marker.help: Do not require magic marker when encoding and do not search for marker when decoding.

--no-prefix.help: Does not automatically add numeric prefixes in reverse mode

--no-prepend.help: By default, if decompression fails, the unit attempts to prefix the data with all possible values of a single byte and decompress the result. This behavior can be disabled with this flag.

--no-wildcards.help: Do not allow wildcards in search string

--not.help: Hide the given chunks instead of making them the only ones visible.

--only-ascii.help: Search for ASCII encoded patterns only.

--only-utf16.help: Search for UTF16 encoded patterns only.

--or.help: Any keywords may match rather than requiring all of them to match.

--oracle.help: node oracle: batched vm (fast, default) or per-process (canonical, ~10x slower)

--out.help: write div_/crash_/dirty_ artifact files into DIR

--pick.help: Pick the pattern occurrence at index k, starting at 0.

--plus.help: also replace plus signs by spaces

--prefix.help: optionally select a prefix that every refinery command will receive

--prologue.help: Optional expression with which the state variable S is updated before a block is operated on.

--protocol.help: Escape the protocol colon in URLs.

--quote.help: Wrap all indicators in backticks for markdown code.

--scoped.help: Prevent sep from automatically turning all input chunks visible.

--seed.help: Optional seed value for the state variable S. The default is zero.

--size.help: If specified, files will be read in chunks of size N and each chunk is emitted as one element in the output list.

--sort.help: Sort the resourcey by name rather than by order of appearance.

--stream.help: Dump all incoming inputs to the same file.

--take.help: The number of bytes to read.

--tolerance.help: Decompress will attempt to strip up to n bytes from the beginning of the data. The default is 12.

--truncate.help: Truncate possible excess bytes at the end of the input, by default they are appended as a single chunk.

--try.help: Silence exceptions and return input data if no output would be produced.

--unicode.help: Expect input/output to be an UTF-8 encoded unicode string and use unicode escape sequences.

--url-only.help: Only defang URLs, do not look for domains or IPs.

--utf16.help: Read the memory at the given offset as an UTF16 string.

--version.help: Only show the currently installed version of binary refinery and exit.

--whitespace.help: Strip all whitespace from input data.

--width.help: number of data bytes to put in one row

--words.help: Keywords only match if they appear as words, not as substrings.

--workers.help: parallel worker processes (default: min(8, CPU count))

-T.help: Set the terminal width, the default is 80 characters. Setting the width to zero (-T0) will use the full terminal width.

alphabet.help: The alphabet which should be used, default is the Latin one: "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

arg.help: A single numeric expression which provides the right argument to the operation, where the left argument is each block in the input data. This argument can also contain a sequence of bytes which is then split into blocks of the same size as the input data and used cyclically.

base.help: Find only numbers in given base. Default of 0 means that common expressions for hexadecimal, octal and binary are accepted.

count.help: Defines the number of outputs for each input. The default is 2.

data.help: Data to be emitted. If no argument is specified, data is retrieved from the clipboard. Multiple arguments are output in framed format.

filenames.help: A list of file masks (with wildcard patterns). Each matching file will be read from disk and emitted.

gen.help: print the generated program for a seed

junk.help: Character(s) to be removed, default is whitespace.

keywords.help: Provide keywords; if any of these keywords match the help description of a unit, it will be listed.

limit.help: Optionally specify a number of bytes to read, default is to read until the end of input.

needles.help: A wildcard pattern for the name of a .NET resource. Omit to list all available resources.

offset.help: Specify virtual offset as either .section:OFFSET or just a virtual address in hex.

operation.help: A Python expression defining the operation.

padding.help: Optional byte sequence to use as padding for tail end.

pattern.help: run all tests whose file name contains the given pattern.

refs.help: A sheet reference to be extracted.

replace.help: The substitution string. Leave this empty to remove all occurrences of the search term.

run.help: reproduce and inspect one seed end-to-end

separator.help: Separator; the default is a line break.

slice.help: Specify start:stop:step in Python slice syntax.

subst.help: substitution, use $1 for group 1, $0 for entire match. Matches get removed by default.

sweep.help: fuzz a range of seeds and report divergences

venv.help: Specify the virtual environment to use.
